cases.request: Generate a fixed-base branching manipulator named BranchArm. A 25 kg box pedestal supports a 1.0 m, 8 kg cylindrical trunk through a revolute joint about Z limited to -1.57 rad through 1.57 rad. The trunk branches into a 0.70 m, 4 kg box arm through a revolute shoulder about Y limited to -1.2 rad through 1.2 rad and a 0.45 m, 3 kg box slide through a prismatic joint about X limited to 0 m through 0.30 m. Command all three joints with joint-space PD effort control using proportional gains 60 N.m/rad, 45 N.m/rad, and 800 N/m and derivative gains 8 N.m.s/rad, 6 N.m.s/rad, and 60 N.s/m. Limit the rotary efforts to 80 N.m and 55 N.m and the linear effort to 900 N. Joint encoders report position and velocity. Track targets of 0.6 rad, -0.4 rad, and 0.20 m at 100 Hz for 5 s. Require every joint to remain inside its limits and eventually reach within 0.05 rad or 0.01 m of its target.

Generate a floating differential-drive mobile robot named Scout. The chassis is a 0.60 m by 0.40 m by 0.20 m rigid box with mass 18 kg. It has two cylindrical driven wheels of radius 0.10 m and width 0.05 m, separated by a 0.45 m track width, with continuous revolute wheel joints about the Y axis. Each wheel is commanded by motor torque limited to 12 N.m. A PID wheel-speed controller tracks a 4 rad/s target using proportional gain 2 N.m.s/rad, integral gain 0.5 N.m/rad, derivative gain 0.1 N.m.s2/rad, and receives wheel encoder velocity feedback. Mount an IMU on the chassis that reports angular velocity and linear acceleration. Place the robot on a rigid ground plane with friction coefficient 0.8 and add a box obstacle 2 m in front of its initial pose. Use a 100 Hz controller clock for a 5 s scenario. Require both wheel speeds to remain between -8 rad/s and 8 rad/s, require the chassis pitch and roll magnitude to remain below 0.35 rad, and require no collision with the obstacle.

Generate a free-base quadrotor named Surveyor. Its 1.8 kg rigid box fuselage is 0.35 m by 0.35 m by 0.12 m, with four rotors at offsets (+-0.22 m, +-0.22 m, 0 m). Each thrust actuator produces 0 N through 12 N along body Z and contributes yaw torque with coefficient 0.015 m. Model gravity at 9.81 m/s2 and linear translational drag of 0.18 N.s/m. An IMU reports body angular velocity and linear acceleration, and an altimeter reports height. Use a cascaded controller: altitude PID gains 4 N/m, 1 N/(m.s), and 2 N.s/m target 2.0 m, while roll and pitch PD gains are 0.8 N.m/rad and 0.12 N.m.s/rad and yaw PD gains are 0.5 N.m/rad and 0.08 N.m.s/rad, all targeting level attitude and zero yaw. Run at 200 Hz for 8 s. Require altitude to settle within 0.15 m of 2.0 m by 5 s, roll and pitch magnitude to stay below 0.45 rad, and every rotor thrust to stay within its actuator limits.

Generate a floating-base quadruped named Trotter. The torso is a 22 kg rigid box measuring 0.70 m by 0.32 m by 0.18 m. It has four identical legs; each leg has a spherical hip, a 0.32 m and 2.0 kg capsule upper leg, a revolute knee about Y limited to 0 rad through 2.4 rad, a 0.30 m and 1.5 kg capsule lower leg, and a spherical foot of radius 0.055 m. Each foot has contact-state and normal-force sensing. Track a periodic joint trajectory at each knee between 0.55 rad and 1.05 rad with a 1.0 s period using PD gains 35 N.m/rad and 3 N.m.s/rad, with knee torque limited to 45 N.m. Place the robot on a rigid heightfield terrain with friction coefficient 0.9 and gravity 9.81 m/s2. Use a 250 Hz controller clock for 6 s. Require knee angles and torques to remain within their limits, require at least two feet in contact after the first second, and require torso roll and pitch magnitude to remain below 0.5 rad.

Generate a free-base autonomous underwater vehicle named Pelican. The rigid capsule hull is 1.6 m long with radius 0.18 m and mass 95 kg, and displaces 0.098 m3 of water with density 1025 kg/m3. Model gravity at 9.81 m/s2, quadratic translational drag coefficients of 35 N.s2/m2 in surge and 70 N.s2/m2 in heave, and buoyancy acting upward at the hull center. Four body-wrench thrusters provide two surge forces and two heave forces, each limited to -120 N through 120 N. A pressure depth sensor reports depth and an IMU reports angular velocity and linear acceleration. A depth PID controller with gains 180 N/m, 25 N/(m.s), and 90 N.s/m targets 8 m depth while a heading PD controller with gains 45 N.m/rad and 12 N.m.s/rad targets zero yaw. Use a 50 Hz controller clock for 30 s. Require depth to settle within 0.5 m of 8 m by 20 s, absolute roll and pitch to remain below 0.35 rad, and all thruster commands to remain within bounds.

Generate a parallel-jaw gripper named PinchGripper grasping a rigid box object. The 6 kg gripper palm is a 0.24 m by 0.12 m by 0.08 m box. Two 0.6 kg box fingers, each 0.12 m by 0.03 m by 0.04 m, move symmetrically on prismatic X joints from 0 m through 0.055 m. The object is a 1.2 kg box measuring 0.08 m by 0.08 m by 0.12 m. Give finger pads and object friction coefficient 0.9 and restitution 0.05, with collision enabled. Each finger has position and contact-force sensing. An impedance controller targets a 0.035 m closure with stiffness 900 N/m and damping 35 N.s/m, limits each finger force to 40 N, and then maintains a 20 N grasp force. Place the object between the open fingers on a rigid support plane. Run the controller at 500 Hz for 4 s. Require both finger positions to remain within travel limits, total normal grasp force to reach at least 30 N by 2 s and remain below 80 N, and the object to remain collision-attached between the fingers through 4 s.

Generate a fixed-base six-axis serial robot named PathArm. Use six revolute joints with axes Z, Y, Y, X, Y, and X and limits of +-2.8 rad, +-1.8 rad, +-2.2 rad, +-3.0 rad, +-2.0 rad, and +-3.1 rad. The six rigid capsule links have lengths 0.45 m, 0.40 m, 0.32 m, 0.22 m, 0.18 m, and 0.12 m and masses 8 kg, 6 kg, 4 kg, 2 kg, 1.2 kg, and 0.8 kg. Follow a time-indexed cubic joint trajectory from all-zero angles at 0 s to [0.8, -0.6, 1.0, 0.5, -0.4, 0.9] rad at 3 s and hold it through 6 s. Each axis uses PID plus velocity feedforward with proportional gains [90, 80, 65, 35, 25, 18] N.m/rad, integral gains [4, 4, 3, 2, 1, 1] N.m/(rad.s), derivative gains [12, 10, 8, 4, 3, 2] N.m.s/rad, and effort limits [140, 120, 90, 45, 30, 20] N.m. Encoders report joint position and velocity at 200 Hz. Require all limits to hold, overshoot below 10 percent, and every joint to settle within 0.04 rad of its final target by 4.5 s.

Generate a planar four-bar closed-chain mechanism named FourBar. A fixed ground link has pivots 0.50 m apart. The input crank is a 0.20 m, 1.0 kg box link; the coupler is a 0.45 m, 1.5 kg box link; and the output rocker is a 0.35 m, 1.2 kg box link. Connect them with four revolute Z joints and enforce loop closure between the rocker and the second ground pivot. Drive the crank joint with a velocity PI controller targeting 1.5 rad/s using proportional gain 8 N.m.s/rad and integral gain 3 N.m/rad, with motor torque limited to 25 N.m. Encoders report crank angle and speed and rocker angle. Use a 200 Hz controller clock for 10 s. Require crank speed to remain between 0 rad/s and 2.0 rad/s, motor torque to remain within bounds, loop-closure position error to remain below 0.002 m, and rocker angle to remain between -1.4 rad and 1.4 rad.

Generate a rigid differential-drive mapping robot named Mapper. The 16 kg box chassis is 0.55 m by 0.38 m by 0.18 m, with two driven wheels of radius 0.09 m separated by 0.42 m. Mount an IMU at the chassis center reporting acceleration and angular velocity at 200 Hz, a forward camera 0.30 m above the chassis at 30 Hz, a planar lidar with 20 m range at 10 Hz, and wheel encoders at 100 Hz. Fuse IMU, wheel odometry, and lidar updates in an estimator that outputs planar pose and linear and angular velocity at 100 Hz; preserve camera frames as a separate observation. Drive both wheels toward 3 rad/s with wheel-speed PI gains 1.8 N.m.s/rad and 0.35 N.m/rad and 10 N.m torque limits. Place the robot on a ground plane with friction coefficient 0.8 and three rigid box landmarks at ranges 3 m, 5 m, and 7 m. Run for 12 s. Require estimator output rate at least 100 Hz, planar position error below 0.25 m after 5 s, heading error below 0.12 rad after 5 s, and wheel speeds between -7 rad/s and 7 rad/s.

Generate a double-acting hydraulic linear actuator named LiftCylinder. The piston area is 0.0040 m2 on chamber A and 0.0032 m2 on chamber B, stroke is 0.50 m, moving mass is 120 kg, viscous damping is 1800 N.s/m, and supply and tank pressures are 16 MPa and 0.1 MPa. A four-way proportional valve has maximum flow 0.0012 m3/s and is commanded between -1 and 1. Track piston position 0.35 m using a PID valve controller with gains 7 1/m, 1.5 1/(m.s), and 0.4 s/m. Measure piston position, velocity, chamber-A pressure, and chamber-B pressure. Model hard end stops at 0 m and 0.50 m with stiffness 2.0e6 N/m and damping 2.0e4 N.s/m. Represent the cylinder body as a 35 kg rigid cylinder and the rod as a 12 kg rigid cylinder connected by a prismatic Z joint. Run at 500 Hz for 8 s. Require piston travel within the stroke, both chamber pressures between 0.1 MPa and 18 MPa, and final position within 0.01 m of 0.35 m.

Generate a geared electric revolute joint named ServoJoint. A 48 V permanent-magnet DC motor has armature resistance 0.45 ohm, inductance 0.002 H, torque constant 0.095 N.m/A, back-emf constant 0.095 V.s/rad, rotor inertia 0.0008 kg.m2, viscous friction 0.002 N.m.s/rad, and a 100:1 ideal gearbox with 0.88 efficiency. It drives a 6 kg, 0.50 m capsule link about a revolute Y joint limited to -1.57 rad through 1.57 rad. An encoder reports output angle and velocity, a current sensor reports motor current, and a temperature sensor reports winding temperature. A PID position controller with gains 55 V/rad, 8 V/(rad.s), and 4 V.s/rad targets 0.9 rad, with voltage saturation +-48 V and current limit +-18 A. Model winding temperature with thermal resistance 2.5 K/W, thermal capacitance 140 J/K, and ambient temperature 298 K. Run at 1 kHz for 6 s. Require joint limits, current limits, final angle error below 0.03 rad, and winding temperature below 353 K.

Generate a tendon-driven continuum robot named SoftReach. Its 0.60 m long, 2.5 kg flexible cylindrical body has radius 0.035 m and is represented by six serial constant-curvature sections, each 0.10 m long. Three tendons are spaced equally around the body at radius 0.025 m; each tendon tension is commanded from 0 N through 45 N and measured by a tension sensor. Model section bending stiffness 1.8 N.m2 and bending damping 0.12 N.m2.s. A tip pose sensor reports position and orientation at 100 Hz. A custom shape controller targets tip position [0.35 m, 0.20 m, 0.25 m] with proportional gain 30 N/m and derivative gain 4 N.s/m. Place a rigid cylindrical obstacle of radius 0.08 m and height 0.50 m centered 0.25 m in front of the base, with friction coefficient 0.6 and contact sensing along the continuum body. Run at 200 Hz for 10 s. Require every tendon tension within bounds, tip position error below 0.04 m by 8 s, maximum section curvature below 18 1/m, and contact force below 25 N.

Generate two differential-drive mobile robots named Alpha and Beta in one shared warehouse scene. Each robot has a floating 14 kg box chassis measuring 0.50 m by 0.35 m by 0.18 m, two wheels of radius 0.09 m with 0.40 m track width, continuous revolute wheel joints about Y, 9 N.m motor-torque limits, wheel encoders at 100 Hz, planar odometry at 100 Hz, and a 12 m planar lidar at 10 Hz. Use PI wheel-speed control with gains 1.6 N.m.s/rad and 0.3 N.m/rad. Alpha starts 2.0 m behind Beta in the same lane; Alpha targets 3.5 rad/s and Beta targets 3.0 rad/s. A coordination controller uses relative range to maintain 2.0 m separation and commands Alpha speed correction limited to +-1.0 rad/s. Place both robots on a rigid ground plane with friction coefficient 0.85 and add two fixed box obstacles beside the lane. Use a 100 Hz coordination clock for 15 s. Require robot separation between 1.2 m and 3.0 m after 3 s, require no robot-robot or robot-obstacle collision, and require all wheel speeds between -7 rad/s and 7 rad/s.
